title: Semantic Kernel Plugins & Native Functions
description: Build reusable native C# plugins, prompt functions, and configure automatic function calling in Semantic Kernel.

data.text: In Semantic Kernel, capabilities are organized into Plugins. A plugin is a cohesive collection of functions exposed to the AI model. Functions come in two flavors: Native Functions (ordinary C# methods marked with [KernelFunction] that execute backend code, query databases, or call REST APIs) and Semantic Functions (parameterized prompt templates that call other LLMs). By bundling related functions together, you create clean architectural boundaries.

Any C# class can become a Semantic Kernel plugin by decorating methods with [KernelFunction] and descriptive [Description] attributes. These descriptions are automatically serialized into the OpenAI/Azure function calling schema.

data.text: One of Semantic Kernel's most powerful features is ToolCallBehavior.AutoInvokeKernelFunctions. When enabled in PromptExecutionSettings, the kernel automatically detects when the LLM wants to call a plugin, executes the C# method, feeds the observation back to the model, and continues the conversation without manual roundtrip plumbing.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Semantic Kernel Plugins group native C# methods and prompt templates into discoverable modules
Mark methods with [KernelFunction] and describe parameters with [Description] for accurate LLM schemas
Enable ToolCallBehavior.AutoInvokeKernelFunctions to automate the complete tool invocation roundtrip
Inject services into plugin constructors via dependency injection for clean data access
Handle exceptions inside plugins gracefully to provide semantic feedback back to the reasoning model
data.takeaway: Plugins bridge domain logic and AI reasoning in Semantic Kernel. With [KernelFunction] and AutoInvokeKernelFunctions, .NET applications equip LLMs with secure, autonomous tool execution.
